edits.text: Keep a finite verb (copula/auxiliary or main verb) together with an immediately following short (≤3-word) complement that completes its predicate — e.g. a PP, parenthetical measurement, numeral+unit, exception/contrast fragment, or short object/clausal complement — when there is no intervening comma or punctuation.

- As a last resort, prefer a cut after a short (≤3-word) complement that immediately follows a finite verb (copula/auxiliary or main verb) — for example a PP, measurement/parenthesis, numeral+unit, short object or clausal complement — over placing the cut between that verb and its complement.

- Prefer a cut after a finite verb's immediately following short complement (≤3 words, with no intervening comma) — e.g. a prepositional phrase, parenthetical measurement, numeral+unit, short object or short clausal/exception fragment — over a cut placed between the finite verb and that complement.
